_what_this_is: Mechanical inventory of the corpus as it sits on disk. Facts and counts only, no interpretation. NOT the output of the Profiler agent — the .raw suffix marks this as human-reviewable source material that a person counted. Interpretation and open questions live in docs/notes/corpus-observations.md.
counting_method: every number below was measured from the extracted files; where the corpus documentation also states a number, both are recorded and compared

file_composition.note: two Zenodo records combined by data/acquire/fetch_grascco.sh: annotations+schema from GraSCCo_PII_V2, text/ from the plain GraSCCo record

encoding.json_encoding: UTF-8 (JSON spec); document text is carried inside the CAS as the sofaString
encoding.conclusion: UTF-8, LF, 5 of 63 .txt files carry a UTF-8 BOM

bom_offset_interaction.finding: the CAS sofaString retains the BOM as U+FEFF at index 0, so offsets count it
bom_offset_interaction.worse: in Baastrup.txt and Dupuytren.txt the FIRST gold span starts at index 0, so the annotated surface itself begins with U+FEFF (e.g. '\ufeffARCOS-KLINIK FLENSBURG...')
bom_offset_interaction.implication: stripping the BOM shifts spans; not stripping it puts an invisible character inside a gold surface. Either way this must be an explicit decision, not a default.

pairing.scheme: annotation file per document, text EMBEDDED in it (UIMA CAS sofaString) — not a separate-file pairing like brat
pairing.plain_text_filename: {DocName}.txt  — from the separate un-annotated GraSCCo record
pairing.json_vs_xmi: two serialisations of the same UIMA CAS; JSON is easier to parse, XMI is the INCEpTION native form

annotation_format.format: UIMA CAS JSON (INCEpTION export), NOT BRAT and NOT i2b2 XML
annotation_format.type_system_depth: FLAT string, but the values are themselves compound: CATEGORY_SUBTYPE (e.g. NAME_PATIENT, LOCATION_STREET) — a two-level system encoded in one field
annotation_format.samples_verbatim_note: surfaces quoted above are from GraSCCo, an artificially generated corpus with purely fictional names and dates (CC-BY, openly published) — no real identifiers are reproduced

offsets.unit: character (UIMA CAS begin/end index the sofaString)
offsets.end: exclusive — sofaString[begin:end] yields the annotated surface
offsets.method: every PHI span sliced out of its own document sofaString and inspected
offsets.critical_caveat: offsets index the CAS sofaString, NOT necessarily the plain .txt from the other Zenodo record — see sofa_vs_plain_text below

overlap_structure.note: counted on adjacent pairs after sorting by (begin,end); a nonzero count means the merge policy must handle containment

identifiers.documentId_note: documentId is the INCEpTION curation user, NOT a document key — it is the same string for every file. The filename is the only usable document identifier.
identifiers.stem_parse_rule: stem = everything before the final underscore-delimited suffix, where the suffix may be digits OR letters. Regex ^(?P<stem>.+)_(?P<suffix>[A-Za-z0-9]+)$, applied only where the resulting stem also occurs with a different suffix. The suffix must not be assumed numeric.

_corrected_2026_08_05.cause: The first pass matched a digits-only suffix (Tupolev_1..4) and so never grouped Colon_Fake_A..K, whose suffixes are letters. Same class of error as the MEDDOCAN stem regex — assuming a numeric tail.
_corrected_2026_08_05.note: Amanda_Alzheimer.txt contains an underscore but is a single document with no sibling; a suffix rule applied without the 'stem recurs' condition would wrongly split it into stem 'Amanda'. 16 of 63 filenames contain an underscore; only 15 belong to a stem group.

identifiers.patient_id_evidence: No patient field in the type system. Filenames are surnames/eponyms. Tupolev_1..4 and Colon_Fake_A..K share a stem, which is the only visible grouping above the document. Whether a stem group is one patient is NOT decidable from the filename and was measured from the annotations instead: Tupolev_1..4 carry one name, one birth date and one record number (see below); Colon_Fake_A..K carry 11 distinct names and 11 distinct birth dates. See docs/notes/corpus-observations.md §7.3.

Colon_Fake.NAME_PATIENT: 11 distinct names, alliterating with the suffix letter (Antonia Anderer, Beatrice DE BEAUHARNAIS, CHRIST Charlotte, DAMARIS Dyonisia, Euripedes Erler, FRITZLE Fridolin, GERODLSAUER Gerli, Huberta Hotzenplotz, Iris Iselin, Jakob Jockel, Katharina Korsakoff)
Colon_Fake.verdict: 11 different patients sharing a scenario (colon carcinoma), not a patient

provided_splits.evidence: no train/dev/test directories or manifest in either Zenodo record; all 63 documents ship flat

documented_count.source: Zenodo record file listing (GraSCCo v1.1) and the GMDS 2022 paper

length_distribution.tokenizer_note: whitespace split — mechanical, not a linguistic tokenizer
length_distribution.cas_token_layer_note: the CAS also ships a dkpro Token layer; counts above are whitespace, not that layer
